evidence_label: exact scheduled call/build counts; historical runtime/disk are measured on narrower sets; all-candidate total runtime and peak disk are unmeasured

planned_core.selected_controls: one exact Issue #99 Nominal B=5 set in canonical candidate-ID order per dataset

parallelism.configuration_order: serial; one full source table and one active statistics configuration at a time

ddl_and_analyze_work.interpretation: candidate_sample_row_inputs is the exact sum of statistics objects built times the frozen ANALYZE sample rows. It is a work-count proxy, not CPU time. The pinned PG source uses 300*max(statistics_target), not a sum across objects, so target 300 does not scale the fixed sample with candidate count.

historical_calibration.limits: The 92–473 second scaled range is only an arithmetic extrapolation of old three/five-object runs. It excludes setup/ANALYZE and does not model the larger catalog scan. It is not a total runtime forecast.

disk_and_wall_budget_proposal.total_peak_disk_bytes_status: UNKNOWN before full-universe physical setup and trace sizing
disk_and_wall_budget_proposal.historical_comparison: Issue #107 peaked at 3,969,179,648 bytes with selected sets; Issue #99 DMV's six-worker collection peaked at 14,428,110,848 bytes, but that used six concurrent PostgreSQL clusters and is not directly comparable to the proposed serial single-cluster schedule.
disk_and_wall_budget_proposal.mcv_payload_scale: At target 300, one full ALL state has at most 300 list items per candidate (e.g. 23,400 for Census13). The raw two-column value bytes for two VARCHAR(64) columns would be at most about 11.98 MB at 4-byte UTF-8 per character, before per-item/catalog overhead; actual item counts, TOAST size, and full trace storage remain unmeasured.
disk_and_wall_budget_proposal.raw_observation_storage_basis: 1,440,000-call Issue #107 archive at 121,645,647 bytes scaled linearly to 280,000 calls; expanded blocker traces are excluded and could increase this substantially.
disk_and_wall_budget_proposal.disk_cap_reason: 8/10 GiB leaves about 6 GiB over the highest Issue #105/#107 single-run peak for the larger active catalog, trace and filesystem overhead. It is a safety cap, not a measured maximum.
disk_and_wall_budget_proposal.wall_limit_reason: For a rough stress bound, the slowest historical 280k query-batch extrapolation is 7.9 minutes; the largest catalog is 78 versus five selected objects, a 15.6x list-size ratio per chooser scan, or about 2.1 hours if wall time scaled linearly. Add up to roughly six hours of unmeasured repeated ANALYZE/build, trace and setup margin. This intentionally conservative envelope is not a runtime prediction; stop at six hours and request review if the hard limit is approached.
disk_and_wall_budget_proposal.retry_policy: No outcome-based retry or replacement. A failed same frozen arm may be retried only after a diagnosed engineering/infrastructure fix, within the same caps, preserving all attempts; a change to scope or hard cap requires fresh approval.

optional_scope_increments_not_in_core.status: Not included, not authorized, and not to be added after observing Test outcomes.
